title: Reductivity of the general linear group over any field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\geq1$. Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ be the general linear group scheme of [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Then $G$ is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine group scheme of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, is geometrically connected, and is reductive: for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$, the group $G_{\bar k}$ has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup scheme. Connected has the meaning of [def-weil-connected-scheme], and closed normal subgroup schemes have the meaning of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. For the smooth affine subgroups occurring here, unipotent means that in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation all geometric points are unipotent matrices; a matrix $u$ is unipotent when $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure.

source.place: Example 19.19, printed p.401, with Corollary 19.18 and Lemma 19.16; Section 2.42, printed p.53 (connectedness).

proof.text: Write $P=k[x_{ij}]$, $D=\det(x_{ij})$, $A=P[1/D]$ as in [def-sc-general-linear-group]. The scheme $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine and its coordinate algebra is generated by the finitely many $x_{ij}$ and $D^{-1}$; hence its structure morphism is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its group law is already part of [def-sc-general-linear-group]. By [def-sbc-affine-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], it identifies with the open subscheme $D(D)$ of $\mathbf A^{n^2}_k=\operatorname{Spec}P$, since that open has coordinate algebra $P[1/D]$ and restriction map the localization map. Affine space is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; its restriction to this open is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition].

source.place: Example 19.19, printed p.401 (GL is a group variety); coordinate presentation in section 2.a; smoothness expanded by Stacks Tags 00T7, 01VC and 01VA.

proof.text: For any field extension $K/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $G_K=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$. Put $B=K[x_{ij}][1/D]$. Define $A\otimes_kK\to B$ by $(f/D^r)\otimes c\mapsto cf/D^r$, using polynomial evaluation, the localization universal property and the tensor pushout property cited here. Conversely send $c\in K$ to $1\otimes c$, each variable to $x_{ij}\otimes1$, and $D^{-1}$ to $D^{-1}\otimes1$ to obtain $B\to A\otimes_kK$. The composites fix coefficients, variables and inverse determinant, so are identities by the same universal properties. Both group laws send $x_{ij}$ to $\sum_rx_{ir}\otimes x_{rj}$, so this identifies $G_K$ with $\operatorname{GL}_{n,K}$ as group schemes, not merely as spaces.

source.place: Example 19.19 and Corollary 19.18, printed p.401: the standard representation after algebraic closure; explicit coordinate base change.

proof.text: For every field $K/k$, the ring $P_K=K[x_{ij}]$ is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. The determinant $D$ is nonzero, since evaluation at the identity matrix gives $1$. Thus $B=P_K[1/D]$ is a nonzero domain: the fraction description of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] shows $f/D^r=0$ exactly when $D^sf=0$ for some $s$, hence exactly when $f=0$, and a zero product forces a zero numerator. Consequently the nilradical of $B$ is the proper prime ideal $(0)$. By [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] its spectrum is irreducible, and by [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected] it is connected. Apply this with $K=\bar k$ and step 2 to obtain geometric connectedness of $G$.

source.place: Example 2.40, printed p.52: GL has integral coordinate ring, hence is connected (the item source mistakenly points to 2.42, which proves this for SL).

proof.text: Set $K=\bar k$ and let $U\hookrightarrow G_K=\operatorname{GL}_{n,K}$ be any smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup scheme as in the statement. This is an affine group scheme of finite type: its coordinate algebra is a quotient of $K[x_{ij},D^{-1}]$ (the affine closed-immersion criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]). By the hypothesis on unipotence there is a faithful matrix representation $i:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,K}$ (injective on $R$-points for every $K$-algebra $R$) whose geometric points, here the $K$-points since $K$ is algebraically closed, are unipotent matrices; this is exactly the faithfulness hypothesis of the cited node, which does not require $i$ to be a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-rational-representation-fixed-vector] with $d=n$ and with $\rho$ the inclusion of $U$ in $\operatorname{GL}_{n,K}$. Thus the linear subspace $W=\{v\in K^n:uv=v\text{ for every }u\in U(K)\}$ contains a nonzero vector. Here $n\geq1$ supplies exactly the nonzero-dimensional hypothesis of the cited node; no conclusion about other representations is assumed from the definition of unipotence.

source.place: Lemma 19.16, printed p.401: nonzero invariants; Proposition 14.3 and Corollary 14.12, printed pp.280 and 283.

proof.text:
Normality in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], evaluated on the $K$-algebra $K$, gives $g^{-1}ug\in U(K)$ for $g\in\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$ and $u\in U(K)$. If $w\in W$, then $u(gw)=g(g^{-1}ug)w=gw$, so $W$ is stable under every invertible matrix. Choose $w
e0$ and a coordinate $w_j
e0$. If $n=1$, this already spans $K^1$. If $n>1$, choose $i
e j$. The transvection $T=I+E_{ij}$ is invertible with inverse $I-E_{ij}$, and $Tw-w=w_je_i\in W$. Hence $e_i\in W$. Permutation matrices carry $e_i$ to every $e_a$, so all standard basis vectors belong to $W$, and $W=K^n$. Therefore every $u\in U(K)$ is the identity matrix. This elementary calculation proves the simplicity argument of Example 19.19 in all characteristics, without assuming linear reductivity.

source.place: Lemma 19.16 and Example 19.19, printed p.401: normality preserves the fixed subspace, and the standard GL representation is simple and faithful.

proof.text: The coordinate algebra $C=K[U]$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to the given smooth morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. It is finitely generated by step 4. The restrictions $c_{ij}$ of $x_{ij}-\delta_{ij}$ vanish at all $K$-points by step 5. By clause 2 of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], each $c_{ij}=0$ in $C$. The surjection $B=K[x_{ij},D^{-1}]\twoheadrightarrow C$ defining the closed immersion therefore sends $x_{ij}$ to $\delta_{ij}$ and $D^{-1}$ to $1$. Every element of $C$ is consequently a scalar. Its structure map $K\to C$ is injective because the identity section of $U$ supplies a retraction $C\to K$; it is surjective by the preceding generators. Thus $C=K$ and $U$ is the trivial subgroup scheme. This also excludes infinitesimal subgroup structures, rather than merely showing triviality of $U(K)$. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves every asserted clause of reductivity.
